learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears.

items.title: Starting check: locate the mechanism
items.prompt: An explanation says a student changes an answer after noticing classmates exchange doubtful looks. Which scale is primary?

items.title: Guided practice: classify a structural rule
items.prompt: An explanation attributes regional college access to a national funding formula that allocates resources by district tax base. Which scale is primary?

items.title: Less help: mechanism over headcount
items.prompt: A stadium crowd adopts a chant because nearby fans copy one another section by section. Which scale best matches the mechanism?

items.title: Solo practice: state the blind spot
items.prompt: A macro explanation links housing segregation to lending rules. What does that scale not explain by itself?
options: How rules pattern access across areas
How a borrower reads one lender encounter

items.title: Near exit: choose scale and consequence
items.prompt: A researcher explains workplace deference through employees’ moment-to-moment reading of titles, posture, and turn-taking. Which classification is best?

items.title: Changed exit: read nested levels
items.prompt: A diagram links national licensing law to hospital hiring rules to one interviewer’s questions. Which level explains the broad eligibility pattern?

items.title: Repair: follow the causal verb
items.prompt: The explanation says patrons follow a dress norm because hosts signal approval during greetings. Which mechanism scale is primary?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify a new case
items.prompt: A new explanation links retirement patterns to a nationwide pension eligibility rule. Which scale is primary?

items.title: Repair: name the omission
items.prompt: A micro account explains how nurses negotiate task handoffs during a shift. Which question lies outside that account by itself?
options: How national law sets nurse ratios
How shared meanings guide a handoff

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A nested case shows tax policy shaping school budgets while students form study groups. Which process is micro-level?

items.title: Starting check: identify the lens
items.prompt: An explanation says standardized schedules coordinate transportation, work, and school so institutions can operate together. Which lens is foregrounded?

items.title: Guided practice: identify power analysis
items.prompt: An explanation says a zoning rule protects property values for established owners while limiting housing access for lower-income renters. Which lens is foregrounded?

items.title: Less help: recognize dysfunction
items.prompt: A functionalist analysis of a transit system could include which claim?
options: Transit exists only to benefit one ruling group
Cooperation can never occur around transit
Every transit rule is morally correct

items.title: Solo practice: avoid moral labels
items.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the lenses?
options: Conflict theory proves institutions are bad
Only one lens can apply to any case

items.title: Near exit: match premise to explanation
items.prompt: A school tracking system is explained as sorting students into specialized roles that help institutions allocate training. Which lens generated the explanation?

items.title: Changed exit: predict after control shifts
items.prompt: Workers gain equal representation on a board that sets wages. Which prediction most directly follows from conflict theory?
options: The board will have no institutional function
Representation proves every wage is fair
Worker interests may shape wages more

items.title: Repair: use the premise words
items.prompt: An account asks how family routines coordinate care, work, and socialization across generations. Which lens is primary?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: identify a power lens
items.prompt: A new account says professional groups restrict entry to preserve scarce jobs and status for current members. Which lens is primary?

items.title: Repair: derive contrasting predictions
items.prompt: A public agency centralizes all budget decisions. Which conflict-theory prediction is most direct?
options: Every citizen will receive equal resources
Groups near decision makers may gain

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A hospital adds a shared protocol that reduces duplicated work across departments. Which functionalist prediction is most direct?
options: One group must capture every benefit

items.title: Starting check: identify the lens focus
items.prompt: A case shows one gender performs most unpaid care while another holds most household financial authority. Which question is most aligned with feminist theory?
options: How are labor and power distributed?
Which person has the nicest personality?
How can the pattern be ignored?

items.title: Guided practice: trace an institutional rule
items.prompt: A firm promotes employees who can accept travel with one day’s notice. Caregiving duties are unevenly distributed by gender. Which analysis fits best?

items.title: Less help: move beyond a count
items.prompt: A committee has equal numbers by gender, but one group rarely receives agenda-setting roles. What does a feminist analysis examine next?

items.title: Solo practice: identify hidden costs
items.prompt: A volunteer program praises flexible service but expects unpaid availability during school pickup hours. Which relation is most relevant?
options: Unpaid time has no social cost
Availability is determined only by biology
Gendered care burdens can shape access

items.title: Near exit: map power and labor
items.prompt: In a clinic, women perform most informal mentoring, while senior men control promotion votes. Which feminist-theory conclusion is best?
options: Labor and promotion power are unequal
Vote control has no relation to power
The pattern is only a personality difference

items.title: Changed exit: predict a rule change
items.prompt: A board replaces informal invitation with transparent rotation for agenda-setting roles. What is the most bounded feminist-theory prediction?
options: Agenda access may become less skewed
The change has no possible institutional effect

items.title: Repair: fill the four-arrow map
items.prompt: One group sets schedules, another performs most unpaid coordination, and promotions reward schedule visibility. Which feature should be named?
options: Unpaid work has no institutional role
Power, labor, and reward are linked

items.title: Fresh re-entry: analyze a new institution
items.prompt: At a university, one gender does most student advising while another holds most budget authority. Which relation is central?
options: Budget authority has no social meaning
Service labor and resource power diverge

items.title: Repair: predict the first shifted link
items.prompt: A grant program adds paid caregiving support for required evening training. Which relation should change first if care burden limited access?
options: Training access may become more even
Every wage gap must immediately vanish

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new organization publishes salary bands and requires mixed-gender review panels. Which prediction is appropriately bounded?
